title: Meta-benchmark scheduler for kernel-adaptive runs and staged prefill/decode comparisons
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reusable meta-benchmark scheduler (MB-scheduler) that orchestrates systematic experiments across kernel variants, attention optimizations, and staged prefill/decode schedules, then aggregates results into stable golden baselines used by CI perf gates and nightly sentinels.

Scope:
- Scheduler engine that composes experiment matrices (model variant x kernel implementation x quantization profile x attention optimization flag x workload mix).
- Support for explicit staged runs: prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, mixed-sequence, and rolling-prefill workloads that mimic realistic application traces.
- Measurement suite: p50/p90/p95/p99 token latencies, per-token tail latency distribution, throughput per-second, GPU memory high-water-mark, KV cache hit/miss ratios, and kernel execution breakdown.
- Golden aggregation: combine multiple hardware runs (A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100) into a single canonical baseline that is jitter-aware and documents variance.
- CI integration: perf gate definitions derived from baselines with configurable tolerances, automatic re-baselining flow after approved regressions.

Non-goals: full UI/Console integration (we will expose artifacts as dashboards and JSON reports only in this phase), load-testing of autoscaler behavior (covered in separate ticket).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We intentionally decouple the scheduler from runtime APIs by using the existing perf-runner CLI adapter. This prevents lock-in and allows ad-hoc experiments.
- To keep CI time reasonable we will tier experiments: quick-snapshot runs for PR checks (fast profile, small corpus), nightly full-sweep runs (large corpus, multi-seed) and on-demand golden validation when agents detect a signal.
- Kernel candidate sampling: start with full enumeration for small models (<= 7B), then use stratified sampling for large families (13B+) to limit combinatorial explosion.
- Prefill scheduling: implement staged windows that mirror real app behavior: long context prefill (1000+ tokens), short burst prefill (10-64 tokens), and incremental prefill where prefill and decode overlap to replicate streaming workloads.

Outputs:
- JSON artifacts per run and aggregated baseline JSON in /rt-perf/goldens/ (S3 link in comments).
- Dashboard panels in Grafana with historical baselines and drift alerts (links in comments).
- CI perf gate job that marks PRs red when a flagged regression crosses the configured tolerance.

Why this matters: Kernel routing and attention micro-optimizations have non-linear interactions with prefill/decode schedules. We need a disciplined experiment harness to avoid regression surprises when rolling new kernels or attention patches into runtime. This ticket creates the control plane for those experiments.
acceptance_criteria: MB-scheduler prototype can launch an experiment matrix (min: 3 kernel variants x 2 attention flags x 3 workload types) and produce a consolidated JSON report
Staged prefill/decode workloads implemented and validated against replay traces from production (two sample traces included)
Golden aggregation job that takes nightly runs and updates baseline JSON with computed mean/median and variance metadata
CI perf gate job defined: PR snapshot run + threshold check against current golden; failing PRs must automatically comment with link to raw artifact and suggested rollback candidate
Documentation ready: runbook for adding new kernel candidates and a re-baselining checklist
Performance regression false-positive rate reduced by at least 30% on historical test set compared to ad-hoc snapshots (measured in pilot)
comments: 2025-11-06 - Kickoff: scoped with RT perf, Kernel team, and Platform CI owners. Action: Diego to prototype matrix runner adapter. (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/MB-scheduler+Overview)

2025-12-02 - Prototype v0.1 landed: perf-runner adapter + YAML experiment manifest. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289 (review feedback: add deterministic seeds and avoid taking GPU clocks as ground truth)

2026-01-15 - Pilot run on A100-40GB and H100: identified a regression in KV cache eviction when the new kernel uses fused-attention. Logged follow-up ENG-42301. Artifacts: s3://redwood-rt-perf/pilot/ENG-42109/

2026-02-08 - CI gating proposal reviewed with infra: propose 2.5% p95 token latency tolerance for snapshot runs and 5% tolerance for nightly aggregated baselines. See RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/rt-mb-scheduler-rfc

2026-02-28 - UX: added automated PR comments template and link to triage dashboard. Diego implemented job that posts summary JSON to PR threads. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-config/pull/72

2026-03-10 - Stability improvements: added jitter-aware baseline aggregation (median with trimmed-mean) to reduce sensitivity to noisy runs. Nightly sentinel enabled for 'prefill-heavy' suite. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt/perf-goldens
